same: BAM M6 on xl330 (kt/R/friction budget, kp_fw=200, target_names_expr excludes passive_*)
obs layout 61D: ang_vel3 + proj_grav3 + joint_pos14 + joint_vel14 + last_action14 + twist3 + head4 + body6 (verified against the live cfg term order)
DEFAULT_POSE == HOME_FRAME.STAND2 (verified elementwise; actuator order == DEFAULT_POSE order)
control 50 Hz = decimation 4 x timestep 0.005; MuJoCo solver iterations 100/50
differs: actuator delay 3-6 steps in training, 0 by default here (upstream --delay is off by default and untested) -> pass --delay to study it, but see below: it changes the gait
CPU MuJoCo (Newton/implicitfast + stiff friction constraints) vs warp/MJX at train time -> same model, different solver numerics
training uses collisions=(FULL_COLLISION,): every geom pair collides; the CPU scene keeps the XML's `self_collision_only` class for the leg shells
friction DR (FrictionDRBamActuatorCfg) is per-env at train time; here it is the fixed XML value (MuJoCo default sliding mu=1.0)
one robot, deterministic initial state (yaw=0) vs 32 envs with reset_base yaw in (-pi, pi)
no push_by_setting_velocity events here; the eval script drops them too

protocol.note: single robot, deterministic initial state -> NOT comparable with the 32-env eval_velocity_in_sim.py numbers (different instrument).
protocol.fall_criterion: tilt > 70 deg == training fell_over (bad_orientation, limit_angle=1.2217304764 rad). Height does not trigger a fall.
protocol.truncate_reason: training terminates the episode on fell_over and resets, so no post-fall state enters its statistics; rolling through a fall fabricates a velocity for a robot that is on the floor.
protocol.window: speed/displacement cover valid_s seconds = min(requested, fell_at)
protocol.steady_window: last 75% of the VALID control steps

stability.fall_criterion: tilt > 70 deg (== training fell_over limit_angle 1.2217304764 rad)
